To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Handel-C hardware/software codesign methodology is a useful tool for exploring hardware acceleration of radiosity calculations, and that reconfigurable devices can provide significant speed-ups over software implementations.

the Handel-C hardware design pattern enables the exploration of the area and throughput design space of simple pipelines, and that the use of FPGAs to accelerate radiosity formfactor calculation is feasible.

(1) The Handel-C language is an effective means for exploring the area/through-put design space of simple pipelines; (2) A simple pipeline for formfactor calculation can achieve a 7.5 times speed-up on an XC2V2000E FPGA; and (3) The XC2V20000 FPGA is predicted to deliver a 31 times speedup over a 1GHz Athlon PC for the same pipeline.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework for exploring the area/through-put design space, using reconfigurable devices.

the use of reconfigurable hardware to accelerate computer graphics algorithms and, in particular, the use of a parameterised hardware pattern to enable the rapid exploration of the hardware design space.
exploring how the performance of radiosity can be enhanced using reconfigurable devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FPGAs can be used to accelerate radiosity calculations, and in some cases can be more effective than using the CPU.
FPGAs are a promising platform for the acceleration of radiosity formfactor determination.

reconfigurable hardware is a very promising technology for accelerating radiosity calculations, but the technology is still in a relatively immature state and further research is necessary to determine its full potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reconfigurable hardware is an excellent platform for the acceleration of radiosity calculations.
reconfigurable platforms are a promising technology for speeding up radiosity calculations.
, while reconfigurable hardware is a promising technology for graphics acceleration, it is not yet mature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Handel-C pattern is a useful abstraction for exploring the design space of a simple hardware pipeline.
the Handel-C design pattern can be used to rapidly explore the area/throughputspace of simple pipelined algorithms.
reconfigurable computing is a promising approach for speeding up the radiosity formfactor calculation step, and we hope that the techniques and tools described here will help others in the field.
